Your LSAT score of 42 was the third most influential factor, and because it is above the accepted-student average of about 37, it actually pushed toward a pass prediction. It was simply not strong enough to outweigh the two academic-rank signals.

Your gender and race were not used in this prediction. Family income, full-time status, and undergraduate GPA were not among the top three drivers; your 3.00 GPA is slightly below the accepted average of 3.23 but played a smaller role than the rank measures.

Next, ask admissions for feedback, focus on strengthening your academic record and bar-exam readiness, and seek advising before reapplying or choosing another program. If you reapply, provide evidence of improved academic performance and a clear preparation plan.
